## Body

This adds tmux-specific lifecycle detail to the existing bounds-versus-deadlines note.

At #275 head 10c8debed4cd5a46080ca96fda669f8c69140298, the detached blocking worker holds only the tmux Arc and runtime handle, not a registry, caller or revive continuation; its late result is discarded (crates/daemon/src/http/revive.rs:380-393). Per-command reply channels/FIFO consumption and original-client Arc checks prevent crossing reply ownership or clearing a replacement client (crates/tmux/src/control.rs:245-281,383-419,444-462).

Abandonment is NOT zero shared-state mutation: existing cleanup can clear original control-client bookkeeping and kill/reap that client. query_live uses may_start=false, so the wait cannot start/restart a client; it does not alter seat authority. Unknown ends waiting, then the unchanged locked process/pane decision runs.

REPLY_TIMEOUT's three seconds bound reply reception, NOT mutex acquisition, pipe writes or child reaping (control.rs:171-175,245-291,397-410). Started blocking tasks cannot be cancelled. Sequential reads leave at most one unfinished worker per abandoned invocation, not globally; repeated timeouts can accumulate workers under a stuck control path. Record this as C34 follow-up R275-FU-01, not a new security block absent a normal-use regression under C33.

Proof improvement: measure complete worker lifetime/outstanding workers separately from HTTP response latency. A test's total duration may include runtime teardown waiting for detached work.
